verdict.summary: The Subscription Optimization feature violates data protection regulations in India due to the lack of explicit user consent for tracking viewing activity and credit card information collection. Implement valid consent mechanisms and comply with data protection regulations.

issues.title: Lack of Explicit User Consent
issues.description: The feature collects personal data (watch history) without explicit user consent, which is a requirement under the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019 in India.
issues.impact: GDPR-like fines and damage to reputation
issues.remediation: Implement an opt-in mechanism for data collection during the auto-enrollment process.

issues.title: Insufficient Data Protection Measures
issues.description: The Information Technology (Reasonable security practices and procedures and sensitive personal data or information) Rules, 2011 in India require organizations to implement reasonable security practices to protect sensitive personal data or information. The current implementation does not provide sufficient protection for the collected user data.
issues.impact: Breaches of user data and subsequent fines or legal action
issues.remediation: Implement robust security measures to protect the collected personal data.

evidence_cited.citation: The Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019, Section 35(1)(a)
evidence_cited.content: Valid consent from users for processing their personal data.

evidence_cited.source: Information Technology (Reasonable security practices and procedures and sensitive personal data or information) Rules, 2011
evidence_cited.citation: The Information Technology Act, 2000 - IT (Reasonable security practices and procedures and sensitive personal data or information) Rules, 2011.
evidence_cited.content: Implement reasonable security practices to protect sensitive personal data or information.
